Thursday evenings at the repair café — whether to open a second night (captain review, 2026-02-02)

For: the café's coordinating group, who decide how the volunteers' time and the $6K grant are spent, and who know the Saturday sessions well.

The answer

Open a second session on Thursday evenings for 10 weeks, run by the Thursday crew of 5 fixers and paid from the $6K grant: $2.4K of it. Saturdays turn 31 people away a month; a second night is the cheapest way to see them. The hall is free on Thursdays until June.

Where things stand

MonthSaturday visitsRepairs finished
November11271

  • 31 people were turned away in January: the queue closed at 13:00.
  • 5 fixers said they could do Thursdays:
    • 3 of them repair lamps, radios and kettles,
    • 2 repair bikes.
  • About 64 % of January's visits ended in a finished repair (80 of 124).

Where the figures come from

The visit counts are the door tally; the repairs are the fixers' own log, kept in the sign-in sheet and summarised at https://example.com/repair-cafe/tally. Read more on the method at the network's guide.

"We left with the lamp still broken, and came back the next month." — a visitor's card, January

The options

A — Open Thursday evenings for 10 weeks

  • You get at the end: 10 more sessions, and a count of who comes on a weekday evening.
  • It costs: $2.4K of the grant: the hall at $240 a night for 10 nights, tea included.
  • It needs from you: a yes by 9 February, and one of you at the first night.
  • The one risk: the crew tires by week 6; we would see it in the sign-in sheet first.

B — Run Saturdays two hours longer

  • You get at the end: the same visitors, seen later in the day.
  • It costs: $1.2K: the hall's longer booking.
  • It needs from you: a word with the hall's committee.
  • The one risk: the fixers who come on Saturdays already leave at 13:00.

C — Keep one session and book visits ahead

  • You get at the end: no queue, and fewer walk-ins.
  • It costs: nothing in money; a booking form to look after.
  • It needs from you: nothing.
  • The one risk: the visitors who never book stop coming.

The best three

Ranked by what the group cares about most: people seen, then the volunteers' time.

  1. A — the only option that sees the 31 people a month.
  2. C — free, but it trades the queue for fewer visits.
  3. B — it asks the same people for more hours.
